title: Integration Architect Risk & Fallback Canvas (WIP)
summary: One-page slide deck to help field engineers and integration architects quickly qualify operational risk and propose fallback strategies during sales conversations and technical scoping. Pocketable canvas: risk profile, thresholds, fallback ladder, canary plan, sample API flows and objection scripts.
slides: Slide 1 — Purpose & How to use: Quick intro: use this canvas when qualifying a pilot/integration. Not a final design; outputs to handoff to infra/solutions team. Triage in 5-10 minutes with customer technical lead.

Slide 2 — Customer risk profile (fill in): Data sensitivity: LOW / MED / HIGH. Latency tolerance: <100ms / <250ms / <1s. Throughput: bursty <50 qps / steady 50-500 qps / >500 qps. Availability SLO required: 99.9% / 99.95% / 99.99+%. Regulatory constraints: PII, PCI, HIPAA, GDPR note. Examples of quick answers to push the conversation: 'Can you list the PII categories we expect in prompts?' 'Do you need retention disabled or private deployment?'

Slide 3 — Fallback ladder (recommended order): Primary model (hosted low-latency variant) -> Lower-cost quantized variant -> Regional fallback (nearest compatible region) -> Cached responses / last-known-good -> Degraded feature mode (e.g., short answers or no function calls). Include an operations owner and auto-fallback budget cap.

Slide 4 — Routing decision matrix (sketch): If latency <=100ms and qps <=200 => prefer n1-low-latency; If latency OK up to 250ms and cost sensitivity high => prefer quantized v2 with batching; If data residency required => private deployment candidate. Add quick routing policy pseudo config: 'primary: model-A; fallback: model-A-quant8; condition: 95th latency >250ms OR cost-per-1000-tokens > $X'.

Slide 5 — Canary + Rollout recipe (technical): Canary size: 0.5-5% traffic for 24-72h. Metrics to track: token latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, hallucination rate on seeded prompts. Automatic rollback triggers: error rate >2x baseline or >=0.5% new hallucination regressions in eval set. Communication: Slack alert + Pager duty if canary triggers and owner not acked.

Slide 6 — Sample API flow variations (snippets to show to customer): 1) Client -> Redwood hosted (model A) -> if timeout -> retry with model-A-quant8 -> if still fails -> return cached concise answer. 2) Client -> Private VPC endpoint -> if region outage -> route to Dedicated in alternate region with reduced feature flags.

Slide 7 — Qualification checklist (quick): 1) Who owns infra? 2) Expected max qps and typical qps? 3) Latency SLA needed? 4) Data residency/retention? 5) Budget sensitivity? 6) Existing LLM integrations? 7) Security/compliance gating? Use this to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Slide 8 — Common objections + concise rebuttals for SEs: 'We can’t tolerate model regressions' -> 'We run canaries + eval sets and automatic rollback; we can pin versions and disable auto-rollouts.' 'Cost is primary' -> 'Suggest quantized variants, batching, and cache-first patterns; we can model unit economics in 30 minutes.' 'Latency spikes during peaks' -> 'Use reserved Dedicated pools + autoscaling policies; set policy to fallback to nearby region with predictable tail latencies.'

Slide 9 — Demo checklist for a pilot (ops-focused): config: model pin, routing policy, cache keys, canary % and duration, alert thresholds, KMS key id (if private), monitoring dashboard snapshot link, handoff ticket to SRE with runbook + rollback steps.

Slide 10 — Next steps & owners: 1) Capture answers to qualification checklist (owner: AE/SE) 2) Draft routing + fallback policy (owner: SE/Solutions) 3) Create canary ticket (owner: Platform Eng) 4) Schedule 1-hr runbook walkthrough with customer (owner: CSM).

Slide 11 — Open Questions (to close in tech scoping): Is the customer comfortable with quantized model outputs for Tier 1 flows? What percent of requests include PII? Are there legal controls requiring audit logs stored in customer KMS?

Slide 12 — Tiny scripts & phrases to use on calls: 'If this is a compliance blocker, we can run a private proof-of-concept in your VPC for the pilot.' 'We typically recommend a 48–72 hour canary at 1–3% before increasing traffic.' 'For cost-first pilots, we can start with a quantized model plus prefix caching to demonstrate unit economics.'
